REVIEW PETITION (C) NO. _________/2026 
(@Diary No.38193 of 2025) 
 
IN 
 
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (C) NO. 12174 OF 2025 
 
SHIV SHANKAR    ……….PETITIONER(S) 
 
VERSUS 
 
CENTRAL COUNCIL FOR 
RESEARCH IN AYURVEDIC 
SCIENCES AND ORS. 
 
    ……….RESPONDENTS(S) 
 
O R D E R 
 
 
   Review petitioner had filed a writ petition before the 
High court of Delhi at New Delhi (briefly ‘the High Court’ 
hereinafter) seeking enforcement of the agreement dated 
16.12.2015 entered into between him and the Central Council 
for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences. Relevant portion of the 
agreement reads thus: 
1. Sh. Shiv Shankar will disclose the formulation, its 
ingredients and SOPs ( Standard operating procedure ) in 
the agreement made between him and the Director 
General, CCRAS, New Delhi Annexed at page 4. 
2. The product and process has already been 
patented (patent no. 238290 dated 28.01.2010) for “AN 

--- Page 291 ---
2 
ANTI-FERTILITY COMPOSITION” by the claimant Sh. 
Shiv Shankar, it is now essential that that amendment in 
the patent has to be submitted by the claimant in the 
patent office for inclusion of the name of the CCRAS in 
the patent. 
3. CCRAS shall develop the product from the 
formulation provided by the claimant which will include 
standardization, pre -clinical and clinical studies etc. for 
which Sh. Shiv Shankar will provide the SOPs (Standard 
operating procedure) and other details as and when 
required by CCRAS. 
4. The disclosed information is to be kept confidential 
by both the parties for which agreement of non-disclosure 
will be signed. 
5. The sharing of the benefits if any out of this 
product thus developed will be shared equally by CCRAS 
and Sh. Shiv Shankar through NRDC  (National Research 
Development Corporation) share. 
6. The commercialization of the product will be the 
joint responsibility of the CCRAS and Sh. Shiv Shankar 
through NRDC. 
7. If any adverse effect other than what is claimed is 
observed at any stage during the trial; the study will be 
discontinued as per prevailing guidelines with intimation 
to claimant. 
 
2.  The writ petition was registered as W.P.(C) No. 
6938 of 2022. Learned Single Judge vide the order dated 
04.05.2022 dismissed the said writ petition by holding that the 

--- Page 292 ---
3 
dispute being purely contractual in nature cannot be enforced 
by invoking the writ jurisdiction of the High Court. 
3.  Thereafter, LPA No. 504 of 2022 was filed by the 
review petitioner. By the order dated 02.09.2022, the Division 
Bench dismissed the writ appeal by giving liberty to the review 
petitioner to avail the appropriate remedy under the civil law. 
Relevant portion of the order dated 02.09.2022 reads as  
follows: 
7. It is true that even contractual matters can be 
looked into by this Court in exercise of powers conferred 
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. However, 
every matter has to  be considered in the facts & 
Circumstances of each case. The facts of the present case 
also indicates that the parties have to establish their case 
by adducing evidence, and in the facts of the present 
case, the Writ Petition cannot be entertained. 
8. In the considered opinion of this Court, the 
appropriate remedy available to the Appellant is to file a 
Suit where all disputed questions of facts can be looked 
into and not a Writ Petition, and therefore, this Court is 
of the opinion that the learned Single Judge was justified 
in dismissing the Writ Petition. 
 
4.  The special leave petition filed by the review 
petitioner against the order dated 02.09.2022 came to be 

--- Page 293 ---
4 
dismissed by this Court vide the order dated 28.04.2025 in the 
following manner: 
  Heard the learned senior counsel appearing for the 
petitioner. 
  Delay condoned. 
  We agree with the view taken by the High Court 
that this is not a fit case to invoke Article 226 of the 
Constitution of India. The Special Leave Petition is 
accordingly dismissed. 
  However, the other remedies are kept open. 
  Pending application also stands disposed of. 
 
5.  We have perused the review petition  and the 
materials on record. We do not find any error  apparent on the 
face of the record or any justifiable reason for reviewing our 
order dated 28.04.2025. 
6.  Review petition is accordingly dismissed. 
 
...……………..J. 
(Ujjal Bhuyan)

(Atul S. Chandurkar) 
New Delhi;

impugned judgment directing all contentions to be taken up 
in an appeal from that order. We issued notice on the limited 
question of hearing afforded, before the order was passed; 
especially in view of the orders of the High Court in the 
earlier round, which specifically directed an opportunity of 
hearing. 

--- Page 306 ---
Page 2 of 3 
 
 
2. Sri Arvind P. Datar, learned Senior Counsel appearing 
for the petitioner sought to argue the issue on merits. Sri S. 
Dwarakanath, learned Additional Solicitor  General on the 
other hand fairly conceded that the opportunity of hearing 
was not granted. 
3. The order dated 29.03.2025 is produced as Ex.P19 
wherein the operative portion is noticed in paragraph 5 , 
which specifies a reasonable opportunity of hearing to the 
assessee. On the submission that no such hearing was 
granted. We set aside the order dated 29.03.2025 and to 
facilitate a reconsideration, we also set aside  the impugned 
judgment. The petitioner shall appear before the Assessing 
Officer on 29.09.2026 on which date or on any other date 
intimated to the petitioner or their authorized representative 
with due acknowledgment taken, the Assessing Officer shall 
hear the petitioner and pass an order. 
4. We make it clear that all contentions can be urged by 
the parties before the Assessing Officer. 
5. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of without any 
observation on the merits of the matter.

resolved, and the parties have decided to part ways on certain
terms and conditions. Accordingly, appropriate and necessary orders
may be passed in accordance therewith.

agreed  upon  by  the  parties,  has  already  been  paid  by  the
respondent/husband to the petitioner/wife by way of a demand draft

4. The following pending cases shall be closed/withdrawn:-

Ramesh  Jaiswal ”, pending on the file of the learned Principal
Judge,  Family  Courts,  District  Sheohar,  Bihar,  filed  by  the
respondent/husband;
(ii) Complaint Case No.211 of 2025, titled “ Juhee  Ramesh  Jaiswal
Vs. Chandra Shekharan”, pending on the file of the learned Court of

considered for any other  appointment  or  for  any  other  
purpose either within the State of Madhya Pradesh or in any 
other State. 
We also observe that the petitioner’s non-completion of 
probationary period in judicial service would not come in the 
way of the petitioner making an application for appointment 
in judicial service in State of M.P. or in any other State.
The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in the

We have perused the impugned order. Paragraph 6(3) of the
impugned order reads as under -
“6(3) And, further condition that the court below
shall  verify the criminal antecedent of the  
petitioner and in case at any stage, it is found
that the petitioner has concealed his criminal 
antecedents, the court below shall take step for 
cancellation of bail bond of the petitioner.  
However, the acceptance of bail bonds in terms of
the above-mentioned order shall not be delayed 
for purpose of or in the name of verification.”
Learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned 
counsel for respondent No.1/State pointed out that respondent 
No.2/accused has serious criminal antecedents and his role in 
the entire incident is grave and serious. The High Court was 
not right in granting bail to respondent no.2/accused on the 
basis of the aforesaid condition. It was therefore, submitted 
that having regard to the material on record, the impugned 
order may be set aside and the bail granted to the accused may
be cancelled.
Per  contra,   learned senior counsel appearing for the 
accused contended that the High Court was justified in  
granting the relief  of  bail  subject  to  the  terms  and  
conditions that have been imposed and there is no merit in 
this special leave petition.
Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties 
and without making any observation on the merits of the case, 
we simply reiterate what has been stated by the High Court in 
paragraph 6(3) of the impugned order. Having regard to the 
condition  imposed  by the High Court while granting bail to 
contd..

--- Page 406 ---
- 3 - 
respondent No.2/accused, we reserve liberty to the petitioner 
as  well  as  respondent  No.1/State  to  file  necessary  
application(s) before the Sessions Court seeking cancellation 
of bail.
It is needless to observe that if such an application is 
made by either of the aforesaid parties, the Sessions Court 
shall consider the same having regard to the material that may
be brought on record and on merits of the case after giving a 
fair opportunity to both sides to make their submissions on 
merits of the application(s) for cancellation of bail.
All contentions on both sides are left open to be  
advanced before the Sessions Court on the application to be 
filed  either  by  the  petitioner  or  the  State  seeking  
cancellation of bail granted to respondent No.2.
 The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in the 
aforesaid terms.
Pending application(s) shall stand disposed of.

1. The petitioner has been incarcerated on a conviction entered
into by the Trial Court under Section 302 of the Indian Penal
1

--- Page 408 ---
SLP(Crl.)  No.4098/2026
Code, 1860 (IPC) to serve the sentence of life imprisonment.
The petitioner has been in custody for more than 18 years.   
2. In compliance with our order dated 04.05.2026, the State of
Bihar has filed an affidavit with the medical reports.  It is
evident from Annexure A1 that on an examination, the convict
was diagnosed with schizophrenia. Though, it is also reported
that presently there are no psychiatric signs and symptoms and
the convict is well maintained on medication. 
3. We queried with the learned counsel for the petitioner as to
the relatives of the convict; which the learned counsel
undertook to find out. 
4. In the meanwhile, we are of the opinion that the convict
should be examined by a Board of Psychiatrists at the All-
India Institute of Medical Sciences, Patna.  The Director,
AIIMS, Patna shall constitute a Board to examine the patient
and file a report of the Board of Psychiatrists. If the Board
so constituted by the AIIMS Patna; is of the opinion that the
patient has to be evaluated as an inpatient, then the State
shall  facilitate  his  inpatient  evaluation  with  adequate
security provided to ensure that the convict is secured at the
hospital. A report shall be filed within a period of three
weeks.
5. The learned Government Advocate shall also get necessary
instructions  from  the  Station  House  Officer,  having
jurisdiction over the place where the crime was committed as
2

possible, obtain their opinion on the release of the convict.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

Criminal Appeal No………………………………of 2026
(@Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No(s).14147/2026)
ABDUL SAMAD                                        Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF U.P. & ANR.                               Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted. 
2. The present appeal arises out of the final judgment and order
dated  08.04.2026  passed  by  the  High  Court  of  Judicature  at
Allahabad in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 3346
of 2026, whereby the High Court rejected the application seeking
anticipatory bail filed by the appellant. 
3. The present matter arises out of Case Crime No. 474 of 2025,
registered at Police Station Saraimeer, District Azamgarh, Uttar
Pradesh, for alleged offences punishable under Sections 3(5),
61(2), 318(4), 338, 336(3), and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita (BNS), 2023. 
4. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.  
5. Having evaluated the nature and gravity of the accusations,
the civil nature of the primary underlying land dispute, and the
fact that similarly situated co-accused persons have already been
enlarged on bail / granted pre-arrest bail, this Court is of the
considered  view  that  a  case  for  exercise  of  discretion  for
anticipatory bail is made out.  Consequently, the impugned judgment

--- Page 411 ---
and order dated 08.04.2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature
at Allahabad is hereby set aside. 
6. In the event of arrest or surrender in connection with Case
Crime No. 474 of 2025 (P.S. Saraimeer, District Azamgarh), the
appellant (Abdul Samad) shall be released on anticipatory bail,
subject to the conditions I.O may deem fit to impose, on condition
also of continued cooperation in the investigation. 
7. Once the appellant is released on bail by the I.O, on
directions  issued  by  the  I.O.  or  summons  issued  by  the
jurisdictional  court,  the  appellant  shall  appear  before  the
jurisdictional  court  and  furnish  bail  bonds  and  ensure  due
appearance in the trial.
8. With the aforesaid, the appeal is allowed.   
9. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Criminal Appeal No………………………………of 2026
(@Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No(s).13608/2026)
DILIP KUMAR RAMGOPAL TIBREWAL 
@ DILIP KUMAR TIBREWAL   Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF JHARKHAND                             Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted. The present appeal arises out of the final
judgment dated 11.05.2026 passed by the High Court of Jharkhand at
Ranchi in Anticipatory Bail Application (A.B.A.) No. 533 of 2026,
whereby the High Court rejected the prayer for anticipatory bail
made by the appellant (DILIP KUMAR RAMGOPAL TIBREWAL) in connection
with Telco P.S. Case No. 104 of 2018 (corresponding to G.R. Case
No. 2027 of 2018). The said case was registered under Sections 406,
420, 468, 471, and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and
Sections 132(1)(b), 132(1)(e), and 132(1)(i) of the Jharkhand Goods
and Services Tax Act, 2017. 
2. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the
appellant is a registered trader in Maharashtra who made bona fide
purchases from M/s P.K. Traders against valid tax invoices and
proper documentation. The appellant was neither named in the FIR
dated 12.06.2018 nor was he charge-sheeted in Final Form No.
78/2020 dated 15.05.2020 submitted by the Investigating Officer. 
3. Learned  counsel  for  the  State  has  opposed  the  appeal,
submitting that the appellant is involved in an economic offence

--- Page 414 ---
causing loss to the public exchequer by wrongly claiming Input Tax
Credit (ITC). 
4. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties,
it is noted that the investigation in the matter stands concluded
and the charge-sheet has already been filed. The charges have been
framed, and the trial is currently in progress. Considering the
facts and circumstances of the case, the custodial interrogation of
the appellant is no longer required. Consequently, this Court is
inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the appellant.
5. In view of the above, we set aside the impugned order dated
11.05.2026 passed by the High Court of Jharkhand. We direct that,
in the event of arrest or appearance of the appellant (DILIP KUMAR
RAMGOPAL TIBREWAL) he shall be released on anticipatory bail,
subject to the conditions the I.O may deem fit to impose, on
condition also of continued cooperation in the investigation.
6. Once  the  appellant  is  released  on  bail  by  the  I.O,  on
directions  issued  by  the  I.O.  or  summons  issued  by  the
jurisdictional  court,  the  appellant  shall  appear  before  the
jurisdictional  court  and  furnish  bail  bonds  and  ensure  due
appearance in the trial.
7. With the aforesaid, the appeal is allowed. 
8. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.

                                   (J. B. PARDIWALA)
 ……………………………………………………J.
                                    (K. VINOD CHANDRAN)
NEW DELHI;
SEPTEMBER 08, 2026.

alleged in this contempt petition.

patients are duly taken care by the Rights of Persons with
1

Disabilities Act, 20161.

considered in accordance with law.

                             O R D E R
Heard learned counsels for the parties.
2. Though, inter  alia many issues have been raised before this
Court, both on the legal aspect as well as on the factual aspect,
but on one fact which relates initiation of the controversy at
hand, there is still no clarity. The same relates to the fact

--- Page 522 ---
2
whether the Principal Civil Judge (Senior Division) to whose file
the records of the probation case filed by the respondents was
transferred could in turn, transfer it to the 2 nd Additional Senior
Civil Judge (Senior Division) for consideration and disposal.
Records show that the transfer by the Principal Civil Judge (Senior
Division) of the case to the Court of 2 nd Additional Senior Civil
Judge (Senior Division) was subject to approval by the District
Judge.
3. No material has been brought on record by either side as to
whether the District Judge had formally approved such transfer. As
the same would go to the root of the issue, in our considered
opinion, there has to be clarity on this factual aspect.
4. Accordingly, we direct the Registrar General of the High Court
of Orissa to get a report from the District Judge/Principal
District Judge, District Khurda, Odisha with regard to whether an
order was passed by the then District Judge in the matter of
approval subsequent to the original transfer by the District Judge
of the case to the file of the Principal Civil Judge (Senior
Division) dated 03.04.2012 which was followed by transfer made by
the Principal Civil Judge (Senior Division) of the case to the
Court of 2 nd Additional Senior Civil Judge (Senior Division) dated
12.11.2014.
5. The said report be submitted within one month from today along
with the copy of supporting documents.
6. The Registrar General of the High Court of Orissa shall
forward the said report to the Secretary General of this Court in a
sealed cover to be placed before this Court.

suspension of sentence does not arise.

to be suspended.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.       OF 2026
(arising out of SLP(Crl.) No. 12050/2026)
NEETABEN ..... APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
THE STATE OF GUJARAT & ORS. ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1.  Leave granted. 
2. The appellant, Neetaben, is aggrieved by the dismissal of her
vacate stay application by a learned Judge of the High Court
of  Gujarat  at  Ahmedabad,  vide  the impugned  order  dated
08.12.2025. 
3. The interim order, which was the subject matter of the vacate
stay application filed by the appellant, was with regard to
the interim order of stay of further proceedings against
respondent Nos. 2 to 4, viz., Vibhaben Nayan, Hina Nayan Mehta
and Minal Nayan Mehta, in the quash petition filed by them. 
4. Respondent Nos. 2 to 4 are the mother-in-law and sisters-in-
law of the appellant and their quash petition was in relation
to  the  criminal  proceedings  instituted  by  the  appellant
arising out of her matrimonial disputes with her husband and
her in-laws. 
5. We find from the impugned order that the learned judge merely
referred to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for
1

--- Page 558 ---
the parties, but voiced no specific reason as to why he was of
the opinion that the appellant had failed to make out a case
for vacating of the interim relief granted in favour of
respondent Nos. 2 to 4. 
6. It was incumbent upon the learned judged to record the reasons
as to why dismissal of the vacate stay application filed by
the appellant was warranted on facts and in law.  It does not
suffice to merely record an ipse dixit statement to the effect
that the appellant had failed to make out a case for vacating
of the stay with nothing further.
7. The order impugned is set aside on this short ground and
Criminal Misc. Application (for vacating interim relief) No.
1/2025 in R/Special Criminal Application No. 233/2024 is
restored to the file of the High Court for consideration
afresh on merits and in accordance with law.  A reasoned order
shall be passed upon completion of the said exercise. 
8. We make it clear that we have not gone into the merits of the
matter and all issues are left open to be considered by the
High Court in the said application. 
9. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed in the aforestated terms. 
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of. 
.....................J.
(SANJAY KUMAR)
.....................J.
(SANJEEV SACHDEVA)

A W A R D
1. The parties have reached a settlement on 25th June, 2026, which has been
forwarded to this Court by Mr. Sunit Aggarwal, Member Secretary, District Legal
Services Authority, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. 
2. Appellant has been convicted for offence punishable under Section 138 of
the Negotiable Instruments Act, 18811.
3. In course of pendency of the criminal appeal, the parties have agreed that
the respondent would have no objection to compounding of the offence upon
payment of Rs.3,29,000/- (Rupees Three lakh twenty nine thousand) only to
1 NI Act
1

--- Page 961 ---
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (Crl.) Nos.18402-18403/2024
her by the petitioner.
4. We have interacted with the respondent. She is aware that an amount of
Rs.3,29,000 (Rupees Three lakh twenty nine thousand) only has been deposited
by the petitioner before the trial court. 
5. In  terms  of  the settlement agreement, the  respondent  is  entitled  to
withdraw such amount. The trial court may, therefore, release the amount of
Rs.3,29,000/- (Rupees Three lakh twenty nine thousand) only with accrued
interest in favour of the respondent not later than 10 (ten) days of an approach
being made in this behalf. 
6. The  statutory  ordainment  of  Section  147,  NI  Act  is  that  offences
thereunder are compoundable. In view of release of the amount directed by us,
the offence under section 138 of the NI Act is compounded and the appellant’s
conviction and sentence shall stand set aside.
7. The terms of settlement shall form part of this award.
8. The special leave petitions, accordingly, stand disposed of, recording such
terms of settlement.

O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, who is the owner of the
vehicle and upon whom the liability to pay Rs. 5,29,800/- (Rupees
Five Lakh Twenty-Nine Thousand Eight Hundred) with 6% per annum

--- Page 1143 ---
2
SLP (C) No. 11303/2024
interest has been fixed, contends that the issue whether  an
occupant of a car  would be covered under the ACT Policy of
insurance is pending consideration in Special Leave to Appeal (C)
No. 3433 of 2022.
3. Learned counsel for the respondents points out that the said
case may not have too much of a bearing on the present case for the
reason that in the said case, the liability  qua the Insurance
Company/Insurer is to be decided, but here the liability has been
fixed on the owner and the claimants, being poor persons and death
having occurred and a meager amount being awarded, the Court may
not interfere in the facts of the present case.
4. We have considered the matter and find substance in the
contention of learned counsel for the respondents.
5. Accordingly, this Special Leave Petition stands dismissed.
6. However,  it  shall  be  open  to  the  petitioner  to  seek
appropriate remedy in case a favourable order is passed against the
Insurance Company in Special Leave to Appeal (C) No. 3433 of 2022.

UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                      O R D E R
The learned counsel appearing for the respondent,
State  of  Madhya  Pradesh,  placed  reliance  on  the
SLP(Crl.) No. 10955/2026          1  

--- Page 1165 ---
decisions of this Court in  Krishan  Kumar  Malik  vs.
State of Haryana 1, which was thereafter followed by a
3-Judge Bench in Sunil vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 2. We
are,  however,  of  the  opinion  that  it  would  be
appropriate that commentaries on the evidentiary value
of DNA testing are also examined, given the report in
this case that the DNA profile of the accused did not
match with the samples drawn from the victim.
The matter is, accordingly, adjourned.
However, given the aforestated facts and also the
length of incarceration suffered by the petitioner,
Sanjay Kol, we are of the opinion that he would be
entitled to grant of interim bail at this stage.  The
petitioner shall, accordingly, be released on interim
bail on such appropriate terms and conditions as may
be  fixed  by  the  trial  Court,  unless  his  further
incarceration is lawfully required in connection with
any other case.
Re-list on 02.11.2026.

ITEM NO.15               COURT NO.1               SECTION PIL-W
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Writ Petition(s)(Civil)  No(s).  1105/2026
ANJANI KUMAR                                       Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA & ORS.                              Respondent(s)
Date : 08-09-2026 This petition was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Pradeep Kumar Rai, Sr. Adv.
Mr. Mridul Saxena, Sr. Adv.
Mr. Saif Rizvi, Adv.
                   Mr. Shivam Tyagi, Adv.
                   Mr. Mohd. Faisal, AOR
Mr. Manoj Kumar Dwivedi, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In this Writ Petition purportedly filed in public interest, an
important issue re: time-bound compliance with statutory Sulphur
Dioxide emission norms, specifically, mandatory installation and
operationalisation of Flue Gas Desulphurisation (FGD) systems, at
Category A coal-fired Thermal Power Plants (TPPs) has been raised.
The  cause  of  action  originates  from  the  notification  dated
07.12.2015 issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and
Climate Change (MoEF&CC) under the Environment (Protection) Rules,
1986,  whereby  new  and  stricter  emission  standards  have  been
prescribed to be applicable to all coal-based TPPs in India.  The
stricter compliance is mandated to be complied with within two
1

--- Page 1267 ---
years.  It is, however, alleged that the time period has been
repeatedly extended and, as a result thereof, immense loss has been
caused, leading to various health hazards, especially respiratory
and cardiac illnesses, as a result of which hundreds of persons are
alleged to have unfortunately died.  
2. We find that at the threshold, the prayer made herein can be
effectively raised before the National Green Tribunal (NGT). We,
consequently, grant liberty to the petitioner to approach the NGT.
Since the time previously extended is to expire in 2027, we request
the NGT to hear the petitioner’s prayer for interim relief and pass
appropriate orders.
3. The  Writ  Petition  stands  disposed  of  with  pending
application(s), if any.
4. It is clarified that we have not expressed any opinion on the
merits of the case.
(NITIN TALREJA)                           (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR
2

--- Page 1268 ---
